title: Sonochemical synthesis of a new nano-sized cerium(III) supramolecular compound; Precursor for nanoceria

material_class.structural_family: tetranuclear Ce(III) building units assembled into a 3D hydrogen-bonded supramolecular network

synthesis.procedure: Single crystals of 1 were obtained by refluxing Ce(NO3)3·6H2O (0.074 g, 0.17 mmol), pydcH2 (0.056 g, 0.34 mmol) and nicotinamide (0.081 g, 0.66 mmol) in 8 mL of water for 1 h, then allowing the solution to stand at room temperature; yellow crystals suitable for X-ray crystallography formed by slow evaporation after two weeks (yield 78%, m.p. >300 °C). Nanostructures of 1 were prepared by placing a 24 mL aqueous solution of cerium(III) nitrate (0.035 M), 2,6-pyridinedicarboxylic acid (0.07 M) and nicotinamide (0.14 M) in an ultrasonic bath (37 kHz, maximum 160 W); the precipitates were filtered, washed with water and dried in air (yield 64%). The sonochemical experiment was also repeated at 0.07 M Ce(NO3)3 and at 40% and 100% of the ultrasonic generator power to vary particle size and morphology.

reagents.amount: 0.074 g, 0.17 mmol (crystals); 0.035 M in 24 mL water (nanoparticles); also 0.07 M in morphology study

reagents.name: 2,6-pyridinedicarboxylic acid
reagents.amount: 0.056 g, 0.34 mmol (crystals); 0.07 M in 24 mL water (nanoparticles)

reagents.name: nicotinamide
reagents.amount: 0.081 g, 0.66 mmol (crystals); 0.14 M in 24 mL water (nanoparticles)

synthesis.temperature: reflux 1 h then room-temperature crystallization (crystals); ambient ultrasonic synthesis (nanoparticles)
synthesis.time: 1 h reflux then two weeks slow evaporation (crystals); sonication in ultrasonic bath (nanoparticles; duration not specified)
synthesis.vessel_or_method: reflux then slow evaporation (single crystals); SONIC 3MX ultrasonic bath, 37 kHz, up to 160 W (nanoparticles)
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Yellow crystals by slow evaporation after two weeks. Nanoparticle precipitates filtered, washed with water and dried in air.

properties.summary: At room temperature, compound 1 exhibits fluorescence emission peaks at about 380 nm and 440 nm upon excitation at 350 nm. Relative to free pydc ligand the emission is red-shifted and is attributed to a ligand π–π* transition.

measurements.conditions: room-temperature fluorescence of 1 vs free ligand
